chunks: From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the slaughtered meat of the Dhimmi (non-Muslim protected person), so he said: Do not eat it, whether it was named (with God's name) or not named.
ai.seo_question: Is the meat of Christians and Jews permissible to eat according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a strict ruling for the meat of Dhimmi, declaring it impermissible to consume whether they recited *Bismillah* or not. This view contrasts with the majority opinion that accepts Dhimmi meat if they are People of the Book, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the specific condition of invoking God's name for the slaughter to be valid. The ruling underscores the principle that mere identity as a Dhimmi does not automatically confer permissibility without the proper ritual invocation.
